name: Montenegro
summary: Montenegro's EV market is small but growing: Monstat counted 950 electric-only and 5,874 hybrid vehicles among 322,241 registered motor vehicles in 2025 (715 and 3,221 a year earlier), and battery-electric cars made up 1.8% of new car registrations. Public charging is sparse and mostly slow: a draft national framework counts 94 publicly accessible charging points with none above 150 kW, there are no Tesla Superchargers, and none of the operators checked publishes per-kWh prices. Only a few firms advertise home chargers and none publishes prices, while household electricity averaged 9.98 euro cents per kWh including taxes in 2025.

home_companies.name: EVC Montenegro d.o.o.
home_companies.what: Sells home, public and DC fast chargers plus accessories, and states that it lays the supply cable, installs the charger and marks the parking bay. Describes itself as the official and sole authorised representative of Schneider Electric chargers in Montenegro; its home range is EVlink Wallbox, 3.7–22 kW (company article of 29.11.2021). Its project list includes two home-charger installations (Podgorica, Tuzi).
home_companies.installation_note: Installation takes 1–3 days, depending on whether the supply cable already reaches the charging spot (company site).

home_companies.name: Gold-m Electric Cars
home_companies.what: Electric-vehicle dealer and service centre. Its chargers page lists a Cenntro AC charger (7–11 kW) for home, office or hotel use and a Cenntro DC charger (90–180 kW), with prices on request.
home_companies.installation_note: The page offers support 'from selection to installation and maintenance' and a quote request; no installation price is shown.

home_companies.name: NEMO-MONT (Solar-Shop.me)
home_companies.what: Solar-equipment company (founded 2007) whose web shop has an 'EV chargers' category (Punjači za električna vozila); no charger products or prices were displayed when checked.
home_companies.installation_note: Installation by certified engineers is offered for solar systems; charger installation is not mentioned.

home_price_ranges.note: Given as 'realistic for Montenegro' in an EV dealer's guide that recommends a 7.4 or 11 kW wallbox; VAT not stated.

networks.name: EKO fast chargers at Jugopetrol fuel stations
networks.size: Seven 50 kW DC chargers announced in December 2024: installed at three locations in Podgorica, in Bijelo Polje and in Tivat, with Žabljak and Herceg Novi planned (Investitor, 11.12.2024). The operator's website has no EV-charging section.

networks.name: EVC Charge
networks.size: Total number of public chargers not published. Example: smart station at the Žičara Kotor–Lovćen car park in Kotor, with a solar carport and battery storage, up to 100 kW and expandable to 200 kW (ecoportal.me, 03.04.2026).
networks.payment: Charging is started and monitored in the EVC Charge app (ecoportal.me, 03.04.2026); the company website says it is working on a digital solution for payment by smartphone.

networks.name: Orion eMobility
networks.size: The Montenegrin page states 'infrastructure of 300 EV charging points in the country' and 'more than 1,000 EV chargers across Serbia and the region'; it is not clear whether the 300 refers to Montenegro, and no Montenegrin locations are listed. The app description (Google Play, updated 03.09.2026) names Montenegro among the countries covered by own and partner stations.
networks.payment: Orion eMobility app or RFID card; cards listed: MasterCard, Visa, DinaCard, American Express, Diners.

networks.name: Motorway rest areas, A1 'Princeza Ksenija' (Smokovac–Mateševo)
networks.size: Pelev Brijeg: four fast chargers installed (RTCG, 22.07.2026), 4 × 50 kW according to the draft national framework; Gornje Mrke: 4 × 60 kW being installed (Portal Analitika, 14.06.2026).

networks.name: Bar solar charging point
networks.size: One off-grid solar unit with battery storage (Beam EV ARC, installed with Beam Europe, Kraljevo) at the car park in front of the Bar marina entrance: 2 parking spaces, up to 4 vehicles at once; power not stated.

networks.name: Destination chargers (hotels, shopping centres, marinas, fuel stations)
networks.size: An EV dealer's guide lists chargers at hotels (Hilton, CUE, Ramada, Splendid, Mediteran, Portonovi, Porto Montenegro), shopping centres (Delta City, Capital Plaza, KIC Budo Tomović) and EKO and Petrol fuel stations. PlugShare shows Porto Montenegro (Tivat) with 3 Tesla Wall Connectors (22 kW) and 3 CEE 32 A sockets (adapter needed).

buildings.topic: Legal definition of a charging station
buildings.text: Montenegro's Energy Law defines a charging station as an interface through which one electric vehicle can be charged, or have its battery swapped, at a given time.
buildings.law: Zakon o energetici (Energy Law), Official Gazette of Montenegro 28/25 and 3/26, Art. 7, point 47
buildings.source_title: Zakon o energetici – consolidated text (Katalog propisa 2026, hosted by REGAGEN)
buildings.source_date: no date on page; consolidated to Official Gazette 3/26 of 09.01.2026

buildings.text: EVC Montenegro's project list shows two home-charger installations (Podgorica, Tuzi municipality) alongside hotels, public institutions and car dealers; no multi-unit residential building is listed.

buildings.topic: Prerequisites named in a dealer guide
buildings.text: An EV dealer's guide lists a parking space 'in a building or a house', single- or three-phase supply, a 7.4 or 11 kW wallbox and protection (fuse and residual-current device) as what a home charger needs. It does not address co-owner approval in apartment buildings.
buildings.source_title: Kompletan vodič: Kako puniti električno vozilo u Crnoj Gori (2025) | Gold-m Electric Cars

policy.text: Under the EU AFIR rules, charging points on TEN-T corridors must be at most 60 km apart; Montenegro's draft National Policy Framework for alternative fuels infrastructure (Ministry of Transport with the Ministry of Energy) says at least 14 car-charging locations along the TEN-T network and 11 truck-charging hubs (27 MW in total) are needed.

The framework, Montenegro's first aligned with AFIR (Regulation (EU) 2023/1804), is EU-funded and prepared by a consortium led by DAI Global Belgium with GIZ and ENOVA; it was presented at a stakeholder workshop in Podgorica on 16.09.2026.

A dedicated Law on Alternative Fuels Infrastructure is being prepared, with adoption by Parliament expected by the end of 2026; the 2030 goal is about 35,000 electric passenger cars with about 50 fast and 500 slow chargers.

The draft framework also proposes a single national portal for permits with legally fixed maximum decision times, targeted financial incentives for charge-point operators, and minimum user rights, including ad hoc charging without a prior contract.

gaps: Home chargers: only three Montenegrin sellers/installers could be verified, and none publishes device or installation prices; the only price ranges come from an EV dealer's guide.

Car importers: Jadran Auto d.o.o. (Hyundai) has a wallbox information page without models, prices or an installation offer; Toyota Montenegro's charging page links to the Croatian Toyota HomeCharge page; the BMW Voli and MINI home-charging pages returned 404.

Checked without an EV-charger offer: retailers Tehno Planet and Tehnomax; electrical wholesalers/contractors Electro Group, ENEL PS CG, Telemont and Vigoris Ecotech. Serbian installers Elektropunjači/Charge&GO and ElektroMil (Niš) do not name Montenegro as a service area.

Did not load: elvod.me (Elektrovod, DNS error), popovicelektrosistem.co.me (certificate error), evcmontenegro.me/products/ (server error 500), paragraf.me (403), pvportal.me (401), epcg.com tariff pages (404; the site renders via JavaScript).

Public charging prices: no operator price list found for EKO/Jugopetrol, EVC Montenegro, Orion eMobility or the motorway chargers; the operator of the motorway chargers (Pelev Brijeg, Gornje Mrke) is not named in any source.

Payment by bank card directly at a Montenegrin charger is not confirmed; coverage of Montenegrin chargers by roaming apps (Charge&GO, Electroverse, Shell Recharge, Plugsurfing, Chargemap) is not confirmed.
Electricity: EPCG's per-kWh prices for the higher and lower tariff were not retrieved; REGAGEN's 2025 energy-sector report (source of the 9.98 c/kWh figure) is not yet posted on regagen.co.me.

Registrations: no 2026 year-to-date count of new battery-electric cars was found. Monstat's quarterly releases (Q1 2026 of 14.05.2026, Q2 2026 of 12.08.2026) contain a table by propulsion energy, but its figures could not be extracted reliably and were not used. The annual Monstat release does not split electric-only vehicles into passenger cars and other categories.
Subsidies: amounts, budgets and deadlines of the 2026 SKLAD E-mobility rounds (published 27.02.2026 and 15.05.2026) were not confirmed; only their dates and closed status were seen.

Apartment buildings: the text of the Law on Housing and Maintenance of Residential Buildings (Zakon o stanovanju i održavanju stambenih zgrada) was not retrieved, so rules on co-owner consent, cost sharing and sub-metering for chargers in shared garages are not confirmed. No building-specific charging rules were found in the consolidated Energy Law text checked, and the distribution operator CEDIS's website shows no guidance on connecting EV chargers.
No company offering a building-level (multi-unit residential) charging or metering service was found.
Method: the web-search quota ran out during the check; the remaining items were verified by fetching known URLs only.
